title: POC scoping: hosted vs dedicated vs private - Apollo Finance
summary: Initial POC scoping to determine deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Discussed success criteria (latency, cost, accuracy), workload sizing, benchmarks, security/compliance needs (SOC2, KMS, VPC), and timeline for a month-long pilot. Action items: Redwood to share pricing and security pack, run a small benchmark on hosted, schedule dedicated capacity estimate, customer to share sample workload and spike traffic patterns.
topics: data security: SOC2, KMS, VPC, audit logs
deployment tradeoffs: hosted vs dedicated vs private
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE. Ethan, our SE, is on as well. Jordan, Priya, Carlos, can you hear us?
[00:05] Jordan Lee: Yep, loud and clear.
[00:08] Priya Nair: Yep.
[00:10] Carlos Mendes: All good.
[00:12] Maya Patel: Great, quick agenda — scoping the POC, capture success criteria, figure out sizing and benchmarks, and talk security requirements so we can recommend hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[01:02] Ethan Shaw: Quick intro from me — I focus on inference runtime and performance, kernel selection stuff, batching, KV cache, quanti- quan-tization configurations.
[01:18] Jordan Lee: Perfect. High level: Apollo Finance is building a risk scoring and real-time fraud detection feature, primary constraints are sub-150ms p95 latency for single-turn scoring, about 200 RPS peak, and strict data residency — some data must stay in EU. We also have SOC2 requirements and KMS for encryption keys.
[01:45] Maya Patel: Ok so latency p95 150ms and 200 RPS peak. Is that online inferencing single token or multi-turn?
[01:52] Priya Nair: It's single-turn scoring, average input length ~120 tokens, output small. Typical seq len 140 tokens including prompt + model.
[02:10] Ethan Shaw: That helps. For those numbers, hosted can often meet p95 if we pick a low-latency variant and tune batching and KV cache, but cost and data residency are the common tradeoffs. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation, and private gives the tightest control for residency but adds ops overhead.
[02:40] Carlos Mendes: On the security side, SOC2 is table stakes. We also need KMS integration — customer-managed keys — and audit logs for every model call. VPC peering or Private link preferred, and we need to understand retention policies.
[03:05] Maya Patel: Understood. We have Redwood Private that can run in a VPC and support customer KMS/HSM and audit export, and Redwood Dedicated supports dedicated GPU pools with VPC options too. Hosted would require us to sign data processing agreements and we can offer region pinning to EU for some workloads. But full customer-managed key in a hosted multi-tenant environment is harder.
[03:35] Jordan Lee: For our legal team, customer-managed keys are pretty much non-negotiable for production. For the POC we can maybe use Redwood-managed keys as long as we validate throughput and latency.
[03:52] Maya Patel: OK that sounds reasonable — POC with Redwood-managed KMS, then production decision will hinge on whether we need Private for CMK.
[04:10] Ethan Shaw: On benchmarks: propose a 3-stage plan — small functional tests (accuracy/regression), latency microbenchmarks (p50/p95/p99 across sequence lengths), and throughput/soak test to validate 200 RPS sustained and burst. We'll want traces for tokens and breakdowns to surface batching effects.
[04:45] Priya Nair: For accuracy/regression we have a set of 200 labeled prompts; we can share that. For latency we also have a synthetic spike trace for simulating 2-minute bursts.
[05:02] Ethan Shaw: Great, please share those sets. Also for the latency targets, do you have a hard p99?
[05:10] Jordan Lee: Not yet, but we'd like p99 under 300ms ideally. p95 is the primary gate.
[05:20] Maya Patel: Noted. On sizing — 200 RPS with 140 tokens avg — that's roughly X tokens/sec, factoring concurrency and KV cache hit rates. Offhand, a dedicated 8-GPU pool (A100-style) should be more than enough with batching; hosted could require autoscale with higher cost.
[06:00] Ethan Shaw: Important nuance: sequence length distribution and KV cache effectiveness greatly affects throughput. If you have many repeated prefixes (e.g., static prompts) cache hits will reduce work.
[06:20] Priya Nair: We do have heavy reuse of templates, so cache hit should be high, maybe 60-70%.
[06:30] Ethan Shaw: That moves the needle. With 60% KV cache hits, effective compute lowers and hosted costs drop. But for guaranteed SLA a Dedicated pool is easier to size.
[07:05] Carlos Mendes: What's the timeline you normally see for a POC? We need to align internal stakeholders and legal.
[07:12] Maya Patel: For this scope, typical timeline — week 0-1: kickoff & data/workload handoff; week 1-2: security review + hosted benchmark run; week 2-3: dedicated sizing estimate and optional dedicated pilot; week 3-4: consolidation and decision. So about a 3-4 week POC.
[07:35] Jordan Lee: That fits our Q4 planning.
[07:45] Ethan Shaw: For running benchmarks on hosted — we can spin up dedicated test lanes, isolate them with quotas, and provide token-level cost/latency traces. We'll need sample payloads and target concurrency script.
[08:05] Priya Nair: We'll provide the labeled prompts and a synthetic traffic generator.
[08:12] Maya Patel: On decision criteria — customer says: 1) if hosted meets latency and cost targets and supports EU residency for production, we prefer hosted for faster time-to-market; 2) if costs too high or residency/CMS keys require, we move to Dedicated or Private; 3) Dedicated if we need predictable throughput and isolation; Private if we need CMK and on-prem or air-gapped constraints.
[08:45] Jordan Lee: Yep that's our thinking. Also operational concerns — how quickly can you rotate models, and what's the rollback story?
[08:55] Ethan Shaw: We support model version pinning, canary rollouts, automatic fallback to smaller models, and tracing to evaluate model regressions. Rollouts are integrated into Redwood Console.
[09:10] Carlos Mendes: About audit logs — what fields are logged and what is the retention? Also, can logs be forwarded to our SIEM?
[09:18] Maya Patel: We capture request metadata, model version, tokens used, timestamps, and can stream audit logs to your S3 or cloud logging endpoint. Retention is configurable; for Private you control retention.
[09:34] Carlos Mendes: Good. For KMS — we need to see the integration doc and confirm HSM support.
[09:40] Maya Patel: We'll share the security pack with KMS/HSM notes.
[09:46] Priya Nair: On quantization, are there recommended profiles for latency vs accuracy tradeoffs? We may need FP16 vs 8-bit.
[09:55] Ethan Shaw: Yes, we can provide quantization profiles and model recommendations. For your accuracy-sensitive scoring, we'd likely try FP16 or 4-bit quant with a quality eval. We'll include expected degradation numbers from previous benchmarks.
[10:20] Jordan Lee: Cost — can you ballpark cost for hosted vs dedicated for our workload?
[10:26] Maya Patel: Ballpark: hosted might run X per 1M tokens; given your traffic and cache hit rate we'd model monthly spend. Dedicated is committed capacity — higher upfront but lower per-token. We'll send a cost model spreadsheet after this call.
[10:45] Priya Nair: Are there competitors you compare against in this space?
[10:48] Maya Patel: We often get asked about major cloud providers and some inference-specific vendors; common names are Anthropic/Claude via managed endpoints, OpenAI for hosted-ish flows, and on-prem vendors for private deployments.
[11:05] Jordan Lee: Our procurement also asked about SLAs and downtime history.
[11:10] Maya Patel: We'll include SLA doc and uptime metrics in the pack.
[11:18] Carlos Mendes: Ok, for POC we'll start hosted benchmarks, then evaluate dedicated estimates. If hosted fails residency/KMS tests we'll pivot to Dedicated/Private assessment.
[11:30] Maya Patel: Great. Any other blockers?
[11:32] Priya Nair: Nothing else from engineering side.
[11:35] Jordan Lee: Legal will need DPIA and DPA drafts.
[11:38] Maya Patel: We'll include DPA template in the security pack.
[11:42] Ethan Shaw: Technical note — please include a small set of logs that show worst-case sequence lengths so we can size for p99.
[11:50] Priya Nair: Will do.
[12:00] Maya Patel: Ok let's recap next steps...
[12:05] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone.
[12:07] Maya Patel: Thanks — wrap up.
